details: Critical, rapid degradation in performance from synthetic data, measured by population risk (expected loss over the real data distribution). "Catastrophic" is often undefined. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Replace paradigm (old data deleted, next model trained only on the newest synthetic data) is "highly unrealistic". Realistic: more compute, more and higher-quality data, synthetic data accumulating beside real data. (Sec. 3, 4.1)
mitigation: Accumulate real and synthetic data instead of replacing it. Population risk diverges under replace, not under accumulate. (Sec. 4.1)
rebuttal: Sec. 5: with accumulating data and larger, higher-quality datasets, population risk will not increase catastrophically. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under accumulate; collapse under replace.
papers: Dohmatob et al. 2024b; Bertrand et al. 2023; Kazdan et al. 2024b
coverage_note: No chart tests catastrophic degradation. The loss chart shows changes of a few per cent when AI text is mixed into human data, which is not recursive training.

details: Strict: collapse if there is any increase in population risk when training with synthetic data versus real data alone. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Not tied to a specific condition in the paper.
mitigation: Not given for this definition. (Alemohammad et al. saw FID rise 2x by iteration 5, then plateau; Gerstgrasser et al. questioned calling it collapse. Sec. 2.2)
rebuttal: Not rebutted. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): collapse occurs under both accumulate and replace. The Sec. 5 forecast covers catastrophic and diverging risk, not any increase.
papers: Alemohammad et al. 2023; Dohmatob et al. 2024b
coverage_note: The loss chart compares loss with added AI text against a human-only control, so a rise is an increase in risk by this definition. Loss is measured on C4 as a proxy for the real distribution, and with mixing, not recursion.

details: Population risk grows without bound over successive model-fitting iterations. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Replace paradigm is unrealistic; real data is not deleted after each model. Realistic: synthetic data accumulates, and real data's share falls. (Sec. 3, 4.1)
mitigation: Accumulate data (shown empirically and mathematically). Accumulate-subsample: loss appears to stabilise, but no theory yet. A real-data share above zero is sufficient, not necessary. Iterative retraining is not used in frontier models. (Sec. 4.1 to 4.3)
rebuttal: Sec. 5: population risk will not diverge asymptotically under accumulating data. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under accumulate; collapse under replace.
papers: Gerstgrasser et al. 2024; Kazdan et al. 2024b; Dey & Donoho 2024
coverage_note: This needs successive generations of models; the WildAI models are single-generation mixes of human and AI text.

details: Variance or diversity trends to 0, and learned distributions become delta-like over iterations. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Replace paradigm is unrealistic. Schaeffer et al. cite about 1 quadrillion available pre-training tokens (attributed to Villalobos et al. 2024). (Sec. 3, 4.1, 4.4)
mitigation: Timescale matters: expected iterations before total collapse scale with data size times entropy. At face value, trillions of models could be trained before onset. (Sec. 4.4)
rebuttal: In that simple model, total collapse poses "virtually no present threat". Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under either paradigm. Authors note the model is simple.
papers: Alemohammad et al. 2023; Shumailov et al. 2023; Bertrand et al. 2023
coverage_note: No chart measures variance or diversity.

details: Collapse if the link between performance and training data size deviates from the scaling seen with real data. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Not tied to a specific condition. Listed in two families: "distributions deforming" and "decreasing value from additional data". (Sec. 2)
mitigation: Further research on how synthetic data affects scaling behaviour. (Sec. 5)
rebuttal: Not rebutted: exact changes under realistic conditions "remain to be determined". Synthetic data could ease a data bottleneck but may alter scaling-law parameters. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): collapse under both.
families: Distributions deforming | Decreasing value from additional data
coverage_note: Both are about the scaling law: what added AI text does to loss at a fixed human-token budget, and the compute multiplier that follows.

definition: Disappearance of or Entanglement of Real Data Mode(s)
details: Synthetic data stops the model learning some modes of the real distribution, or blurs modes together ("mode collapse"). (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Not tied to a specific condition. Real share of data is expected to approach zero, but whether it reaches zero is unclear. (Sec. 3, 4.2, 5)
mitigation: More research on coverage and mode-collapse prevention for realistic settings. Possible idea: sequester real data for later use (labs have already collected it). (Sec. 4.2, 5)
rebuttal: Not rebutted: real tail data and modes will be lost, but how many and how quickly is unclear. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under either paradigm.
short_name: Disappearance or entanglement of real data modes
coverage_note: No chart shows a model losing or merging modes. The web-composition chart describes what the web contains, not what a model has lost.

details: Synthetic data under-represents the tail of the distribution ("coverage collapse"), so models handle common cases but fail on rare ones. Can be subtler than Def. 4. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Replace paradigm is unrealistic, but "very real threats to tails" remain. (Sec. 1, 3)
mitigation: Research on coverage and mode-collapse prevention. Harms can fall disproportionately on marginalised groups. (Sec. 2.3, 5)
rebuttal: Not rebutted: loss of diversity is "a real issue"; how much tail is lost is unclear. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under either paradigm.
papers: Shumailov et al. 2023; Wyllie et al. 2024; Shumailov et al. 2024
coverage_note: No chart measures how a model handles rare cases.

details: Models begin producing fully synthetic data not supported by the original real data's distribution. (Sec. 2)
realistic_condition: Not tied to a specific condition. Example: Shumailov et al.'s OPT-125M result counted as Def. 8; perplexity plateaued 12.5% to 50% above the first model. (Sec. 2.1)
mitigation: Not given. Search providers may pay a high penalty if trained on hallucinated facts. (Sec. 2.3)
rebuttal: Not addressed in the Sec. 5 forecast. Regression case (App. A, Table 1): no collapse under either paradigm.
papers: Shumailov et al. 2023; Alemohammad et al. 2023; Bohacek & Farid 2023
coverage_note: No chart checks whether model output is supported by the real data.
